Sample coverage

Source: R/alpha.R
div_coverage.Rd

Estimates the sample coverage of each site, the proportion of the individuals in the community that belong to species already recorded (Chao and Jost 2012).

Usage

div_coverage(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

unit

For incidence data, the column naming the sampling unit (a trap, bait, plot or survey day) in which each species was detected. Each site is then described by the number of units in which each species was found and the number of units sampled, and every estimate is incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014), for TD, PD and FD alike. Leave NULL for abundance data.

n_units

For incidence data, a column giving the number of units sampled at each site, constant within a site. Use it when some units detected no species and so do not appear in the data. By default the number of distinct units in the data is used.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A tibble with the grouping columns, the site column, n, s_obs, f1, f2 (singletons and doubletons) and coverage.

References

Chao, A. and Jost, L. (2012). Coverage-based rarefaction and extrapolation: standardizing samples by completeness rather than size. Ecology, 93, 2533-2547. doi:10.1890/11-1952.1

Examples

div_coverage(png_ants, .by = season)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 7
#>    season site       n s_obs    f1    f2 coverage
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> <int> <int> <int>    <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200    47    16     5     5    0.898
#>  2 dry    MW0700    23    15    12     1    0.482
#>  3 dry    MW1200    29    13     7     3    0.766
#>  4 dry    MW1700    17     5     1     2    0.953
#>  5 dry    MW2200    13     6     3     1    0.781
#>  6 wet    MW0200    76    21    11     5    0.857
#>  7 wet    MW0700    58    28    17     3    0.709
#>  8 wet    MW1200    57    20     9     3    0.844
#>  9 wet    MW1700    34    10     6     2    0.827
#> 10 wet    MW2200    15     5     2     1    0.876
